1.why: The sans-serif typeface is clearly legible with ample line height on every screen, though letter spacing looks close to standard rather than deliberately generous.

2.why: All headings, buttons, and body text appear in sentence case with no italics, no all-caps strings, and no dense paragraphs on any screenshot.

3.why: The single-column, mobile-width layout with large touch targets and generous whitespace stays readable and uncluttered across all 15 steps.

4.why: Instructions are short everywhere, but a few lines are awkwardly phrased (e.g., 'If this identity can be checked, a six-digit demo code is ready' and 'It will be used after it works'), slightly weakening plain language.

5.why: Every code field shows a format example in its placeholder, such as 'Example: 123456' for the identity/authenticator codes and 'Example: ABCD-EFGH-JKLM' for recovery codes.

6.why: The longest text on any screen is a two-sentence description, so the user is never forced to read a long block to proceed.

7.why: The 'Copy setup secret' button (step 6) and 'Copy all codes' buttons (steps 8-9) let long secrets and recovery codes be copied instead of typed by hand.

8.why: The 'Show QR setup pattern' button reveals a scannable QR code as an explicit alternative to manual entry, with a note pointing to the manual secret if scanning is difficult.

9.why: The screenshots show only plain text inputs with no visible one-time-code autofill affordance or password-manager integration, so autofill support can neither be confirmed nor refuted from what is shown.

10.why: A four-segment progress bar marks the current step and a single full-width blue button makes the primary action stand out on every screen.

11.why: Each screen presents exactly one full-width blue primary button, with all other options demoted to grey secondary buttons or small links.

12.why: Green status banners plainly state what happened and what comes next, e.g., 'Identity checked. Next, set up your authenticator.' and 'Authenticator confirmed. Now save your recovery codes.'

13.why: The user can 'Request another code', show/hide the QR pattern, setup secret, and recovery codes, and go back or retry, with no penalty messaging anywhere.

14.why: The only error observed, 'Your page check expired. Refresh the page and try again.', states the problem and the fix in neutral wording without blaming the user.

15.why: No countdown or reading timer appears on any code-entry screen, but the 'page check expired' error shows page state can expire, so a backend time limit cannot be fully ruled out.
